rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-year (2019-2020) split-plot field experiment at Tongliao comparing shallow-buried drip irrigation (SI) and under-mulch drip irrigation (MI) at three irrigation quotas, with 16S/ITS amplicon sequencing of 0-20 and 20-40 cm soils. Q2: Section 3.4 / Fig. 6-7 and Discussion - LEfSe shows Holophagae, Thermoanaerobaculaceae, Microtrichales, Solirubrobacterales, Myxococcales, Tetracladium, Inocybaceae enriched in SI 0-20 cm soil versus MI; Section 3.1 / Fig. 2 - bacterial OTU numbers in 0-20 cm higher under SI than MI; Conclusion states SI soil is a relatively fertile habitat for beneficial microorganisms.
rows.notes: The study supports only the microbial-enrichment part of the passage. It does not measure plastic residue/pollution, economic benefits, or yield effects of SI vs MI (the no-film plastic-pollution argument and economic benefits are taken from cited literature in the Introduction and Discussion). Single method (amplicon sequencing); correlation with soil N fractions (RDA, Fig. 8) is not an independent method and the posited mechanism (soil moisture/temperature differences without film) is cited, not measured, so Q4 'no'. One site, one crop, one soil, plot scale. Differences between SI and MI vary with irrigation quota (significant at 50%) but no condition is stated as a requirement. No limitations stated. Table 4 and Fig. 2 give means with letter groupings only, no SD/SE/CI.

notes: Full text appears complete. Table 1 irrigation amounts for MI/SI rows appear misaligned (likely typesetting error) but do not affect the rating.
